hypotheses.reasoning: At 08:57:10 catalog-svc-1 failed its liveness probe and restarted (#126). This was a short blip: it was back at 4/4 capacity by 08:57:40 (#129). During that window search-api's CatalogClient retried the 503s immediately, with up to 4 attempts and backoff disabled (#130, #139, #146). That multiplied the load on catalog-svc: inbound rate went 3.2x → 4.1x → 5.0x baseline with inflight around 470–720 (#137, #153, #165), and catalog-svc started shedding requests with 503 'queue full' (#142, #148). Shed requests trigger more immediate retries, so the overload keeps feeding itself even though capacity is fully restored. search-api then runs out of retries and web-bff returns 503 on /search, which is why the alert is not recovering. catalog-db, redis-cache and index-worker look healthy. The index-worker GC pause (#65) and the TLS certificate warning (#57) are unrelated.

Backoff being disabled in search-api's CatalogClient retry policy may be a misconfiguration. It is what turns a brief restart into a lasting overload, but I didn't find any log line showing a config change.
The liveness failure on catalog-svc-1 could point to the instance running out of resources, but the logs don't show why it failed, and it recovered quickly.

verdict.recommendedAction: Break the retry storm. Turn on exponential backoff with jitter (or cut retries to 1) in search-api's CatalogClient, or add a circuit breaker. While that rolls out, rate-limit search-api → catalog-svc or briefly add catalog-svc capacity so the queue can drain. Afterwards, look into why catalog-svc-1 failed its liveness probe, and find out why backoff was disabled.
